references.text: The previous verse describes that the ram must be cooked in a holy place, which is a prerequisite for the meal described in verse 32.
Parallel account of the consecration of Aaron and his sons, where they eat the meat and bread at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
Law concerning the thank offering stating that the meat must be eaten on the same day it is sacrificed, relevant for the ordination offering.
Reference to the bread in the basket—unleavened bread, unleavened cakes, and unleavened flatbreads prepared for the consecration.
Moses instructs Aaron and his remaining sons to eat the grain offering and the breast of the wave offering in a holy place.
Aaron and his sons are to be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting, which is the place mentioned in verse 32.
Paul refers to Israel according to the flesh and their participation in the sacrificial meal at the altar, a practice originating in texts like this one.
The author of Hebrews mentions an altar from which those who serve in the tent are not permitted to eat, contrasting with the Levitical priesthood.
Describes the same consecration ritual; Lev 8:31 gives Moses' command as Exodus 29:32 describes being carried out.
Lev 6:9 establishes the general rule that priests eat holy meat at the tent, which is specified in the consecration ritual of Ex 29.
